transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What has been bothering you or bringing you in today?

With all the changes at work and at home, I just can’t seem to get my feet back under me or handle things the way I used to. Between my EMS company changing my shift schedule and our youngest leaving for college, everything just feels completely disrupted. I'm just having a really hard time adjusting to it all.
When did these work and family changes start, and did your difficulties coping begin within about 3 months of them? Have the symptoms been continuing even after things settled down?

Both the work shake-up and my youngest leaving happened about four and a half months ago, and my struggles started within just a few weeks of those changes. They've been going on for about four months now, but I really believe if I could go back to my old schedule or if home life felt normal again, this would all ease up within a few months.

How much is this affecting your day-to-day functioning—for example, your work performance, relationships, or ability to manage things at home? Have you had to miss work, made mistakes on the job, or withdrawn from people because of it?

It’s definitely taking a toll—my supervisor has already noted my irritability and lack of engagement on calls, and I've had to put paramedic school on hold. At home, I'm snapping at my wife over small things, skipping church, and ducking my fishing buddies to just hide out in the garage.

Besides feeling stressed and thrown off by these changes, have you also been having persistent depression or anxiety symptoms that seem bigger than the situation itself? For example, nearly constant low mood, loss of interest, panic attacks, or excessive uncontrollable worry.

No, I don't have panic attacks or a constant, deep depression that feels separate from my situation. While I've definitely pulled back from church and fishing and feel irritable, it all feels completely tied to these recent work and home changes. I honestly think if those specific stressors were resolved, I'd feel like myself again.
